title: Subtrusive and universally submersive algebraic-space maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with algebraic spaces and presheaves on schemes over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], point classes and Zariski topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and the canonical induced point map [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. Use the constructible point topology [def-sfb-space-constructible-point-topology]. A presheaf map $f:F\to G$ is subtrusive if its point map is surjective and quotient in the constructible topology and every Zariski specialization pair $y_0\in\overline{\{y_1\}}$ lifts to $x_0\in\overline{\{x_1\}}$ with $f(x_i)=y_i$. It is universally subtrusive if for every affine $S$-scheme $T$ and map $h_T\to G$, the canonical projection $F\times_G h_T\to h_T$ is subtrusive. It is universally submersive if for every algebraic space $W$ over $S$ and map $W\to G$, the point map of $F\times_G W\to W$ is a surjective quotient map in the Zariski topology.

source.place: Rydh (author version 2010-03-03), definition of submersions, Remark (1.8), Proposition (2.1)(i), Definition (2.2), and Proposition (2.4)(ii), printed pp.5--8. Read online at https://davidrydh.se/papers/submersion20100305.pdf.
